title: Mobility Visit Coverage by Week
dataSources: Pendant alerts (`care:pendant`), medication adherence (`care:medication`), wandering alerts (`care:geofence`), check-ins (`care:checkin`), care-plan follow-up (`care:ops`).
app: Elder-care and accessibility telemetry — PERS pendant alerts, medication blister-pack reminders, and wandering geofence signals — streamed to Splunk HEC via caregiver apps, exports, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin visit_type=* visits_completed=*
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(visits_completed) as metric by _time visit_type
| sort 0 _time visit_type
description: Trends monthly completed visits by visit type for weekly support coverage.
value: Monthly trend lines show whether weekly support coverage are improving, stalling, or becoming unbalanced over time.
implementation: Normalize `visit_type` on `care:checkin` events and store the fields needed to calculate monthly completed visits.
visualization: Line chart of monthly completed visits by visit type.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Elder Care & Accessibility — typical feeds: Daily activity (`eldercare:activity`), fall alerts (`fall:alert`), medication reminders (`medreminder:event`), check-in calls (`checkin:call`), wandering alerts (`wandering:alert`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `care:checkin`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=care:checkin`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Elder-care and accessibility telemetry — activity and fall sensors (Apple Watch fall detection, motion mats), medication dispensers, and check-in / video-call logs — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and smart-home hubs..

**Author notes:** Normalize `visit_type` on `care:checkin` events and store the fields needed to calculate monthly completed visits.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "care:checkin", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Mobility Visit Coverage by Week** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=care:checkin`) across the full search range. The `sum` aggregation groups by `_time`, `visit_type`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `visit_type`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin visit_type=* visits_completed=*
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(visits_completed) as metric by _time visit_type
| sort 0 _time visit_type
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, visit_type
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.52.27: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Line Chart Of Monthly Completed Visits By Visit Type (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `care:checkin` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=care:checkin | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1m` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1m` buckets.
